items.title: Once high-flying PayPal becomes a takeover target as it attempts a turnaround
items.summary: Stripe and Advent International reportedly made a bid to take over the payments company for $60.50 per share, valuing the company at roughly $53 billion.

items.title: Will PayPal’s (PYPL) Profit Beat and Takeover Buzz Reshape Its Turnaround Narrative?
items.summary: In the past week, PayPal Holdings, Inc. reported second-quarter 2026 results showing revenue of US$8.68 billion versus US$8.29 billion a year earlier, while net income and GAAP earnings per share edged lower year on year. Despite this, PayPal’s adjusted earnings beat analyst expectations, management raised full-year profit guidance, and the company highlighted progress on its cost-savings and turnaround plan amid ongoing takeover interest from Stripe and Advent International. items.title: PayPal Stock Gains After Beat-And-Raise — Why Wall Street Isn’t Chasing Buyout Hopes Like Retail
items.summary: Analysts remain focused on PayPal’s turnaround strategy, while Stocktwits retail traders debate whether the company could command a much higher takeover price.

items.title: PayPal CEO signals deal openness but sticks with standalone strategy
items.summary: Stripe and Advent International jointly recently bid $60.50 per share for PayPal, according to media reports. PayPal's board, with advice from Goldman Sachs and Evercore, signaled that the offer price was too low. With PYPL trading at $58.47 as of Tuesday afternoon, investors appear to be pricing in either a sweetened offer or a credible standalone recovery.
